# ankra_cluster_environment (Resource)

What a cluster is called and what it is for (`ankra cluster update --environment`): its environment label and its criticality, which decides how loudly the cluster reports and how much Ankra's AI may do on it unasked. Both are written in one transaction. A person's own token records the label as that person's choice; a service account's token records it as automation. An ImportCluster file's `metadata.environment` applies only when the cluster is created, so this is how a cluster moves between environments afterwards. Destroy leaves both as they are.

## Example Usage

```terraform
resource "ankra_cluster_environment" "prod" {
  cluster_id  = "0b6f1d2e-1111-4222-8333-944445555666"
  environment = "production"
  criticality = "production"
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `cluster_id` (String) Identifier of the cluster. Changing it replaces the resource.
- `environment` (String) Environment label, 1 to 50 characters, such as `production`.

### Optional

- `criticality` (String) What the cluster is for: `production`, `staging`, `development` or `disposable`. Unset keeps the stored criticality and reports it; a cluster never classified reads as `production`.

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) The cluster id.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# Imported by cluster id.
terraform import ankra_cluster_environment.prod 0b6f1d2e-1111-4222-8333-944445555666
```
